slides.title: Jura Tête de Moine Cheese
slides.description:
The Tête de Moine cheese is a Protected Designation of Origin (PDO) semi-hard cheese made from cow's milk. It is a niche product with a unique consumption. It is consumed in the form of a “rosette”, made with an accessory called a “girolle” which allows the cheese to be scraped finely.

The value chain (VC) comprises pasture-based dairy production, which represents the main area of agricultural use in the country. Milk is produced from cattle on extensive grazing systems, often in wooded pastures. These wooded pastures, representing historical pasture management, are predominant in the region and could help limit the negative impacts of summer drought due to the shade that helps maintain humidity.
In 2020, the VC had 237 dairy farms, 9 cheese dairies and 2 rippers. PDO labelling limits production to two cantons and it is organised by three associations.
This value chain has been selected due to its innovative nature. The project is expected to provide producers with a platform to share their vision for a better future and their knowledge about adaptation and mitigation of climate change.

slides.title: Description of the Reference Region
slides.description:
The “Franche Montagne” region of the Jura Mountains is situated in the Jura canton. This region is characterised by a low population density and milk-cheese-grassland system.

The invention of the ‘girolle’ in 1999, followed by the reorganisation of the actors into a Protected Designation of Origin (PDO) in 1997, positioned the cheese as a unique product in the market and allowed a large increase in production.

The reference mountain landscape of this VC is Corgémont; Cormoret; Cortébert; Courtelary; La Ferrière; Mont-Tramelan; Orvin; Renan (BE); Romont (BE); Saint-Imier; Sonceboz-Sombeval; Sonvilier; Tramelan; Villeret; Sauge; Péry-La Heutte; Belprahon; Champoz; Corcelles (BE); Court; Crémines; Eschert; Grandval; Loveresse; Moutier; Perrefitte; Reconvilier; Roches (BE); Saicourt; Saules (BE); Schelten; Seehof; Sorvilier; Tavannes; Rebévelier; Petit-Val; Valbirse; Saulcy; Le Bémont (JU); Les Bois; Les Breuleux; La Chaux-des-Breuleux; Les Enfers; Les Genevez (JU); Lajoux (JU); Montfaucon; Muriaux; Le Noirmont; Saignelégier; Saint-Brais; Soubey; Clos du Doubs.
The MLR is a region composed of limestone rocks, which are permeable and have difficulty retaining water, forming a succession of shallow valleys and high plateaus. It is covered by forest and wooded pasture.
Milk and cheese production are the first agricultural resource of the massif. Temperature varies strongly between summer and winter and the annual rainfall are abundant (1000 mm).
Clock-making by farmers in the form of peasant clockmakers has been practised since the Middle Ages and offers a cultural heritage to the region.

slides.title: Innovative Nature of the Value Chain
slides.description:
This value chain was first selected due to its innovative nature. Indeed, faced with the significant
drop in the price of milk in Switzerland, the actors were able to organize themselves and develop
a Protected Designation of Origin (PDO) and a unique mode of consumption, making it possible to create value within the territory.
In addition, the value chain is based on pasture-based dairy production, which represents the main area of agricultural use in the country. Wooded pastures, representing historical pasture
management in the Jura mountain, predominate in the region and could help limit the negative impacts of summer drought due to the shade that helps maintain humidity. On the other hand, the
trees present suffer greatly from the drought threatening the maintenance of wooded pastures. It
is therefore interesting to understand how this territory has been able to bounce back from
economic threats and also how it can adapt to current threats caused by climate change.

slides.title: Challenges
slides.description: The natural resources on which the milk used for cheese production is based are threatened by increasing droughts due to climate change (loss of fodder, death of spruce trees in wooded pastures changing the landscape and shade). There are uncertainties about the real effect of climate change on grassland production and animal health (reduced grass growth in summer but a one-month longer growing season depending on the scenario). Counterfeit of the 'girolle' has emerged on the market, which represents direct competition and takes away the unique and innovative aspect of the product. Overall the type of challenge faced by this VC is Current and Predicted. This VC is classified as Traditional and Innovative.

slides.title: Innovation
slides.description: The type of innovation of this VC is Endogenous. The invention of the 'girolle' in 1999 following a reorganization of the actors in a Protected Designation of Origin (PDO) in 1997, represents an innovation since it placed the cheese as a unique product on a niche market (feast and costly), and allowed a big increase in the production. The girolle is a wheel that allows the cheese to be scraped to form a small flower. The innovation is related to New products and New governance systems. The land-use systems involved are Grassland and Forestry. The local assets include Natural, Social and Cultural.

Milk is produced from cattle on extensive grazing systems, often in wooden pastures. Cheese production is based on traditional knowledge dating back to the 17th century. The current PDO organization demonstrates furthermore social resources, such as interactions among farmers and cheese producers, to maintain a sufficient milk price.

ev1654612401030.title: Challenges
ev1654612401030.description: The natural resources on which the milk used for cheese production is based are threatened by increasing droughts due to climate change (loss of fodder, death of spruce trees in wooded pastures changing the landscape and shade). There are uncertainties about the real effect of climate change on grassland production and animal health (reduced grass growth in summer but a one-month longer growing season depending on the scenario). Counterfeit of the 'girolle' has emerged on the market, which represents direct competition and takes away the unique and innovative aspect of the product. Overall the type of challenge faced by this VC is Current and Predicted. This VC is classified as Traditional and Innovative.

ev1654611974123.title: Innovation
ev1654611974123.description: The type of innovation of this VC is Endogenous. The invention of the 'girolle' in 1999 following a reorganization of the actors in a Protected Designation of Origin (PDO) in 1997, represents an innovation since it placed the cheese as a unique product on a niche market (feast and costly), and allowed a big increase in the production. The girolle is a wheel that allows the cheese to be scraped to form a small flower. The innovation is related to New products and New governance systems. The land-use systems involved are Grassland and Forestry. The local assets include Natural, Social and Cultural.

ev1654602704922.title: Innovative Nature of the Value Chain
ev1654602704922.description:
This value chain was first selected due to its innovative nature. Indeed, faced with the significant
drop in the price of milk in Switzerland, the actors were able to organize themselves and develop
a Protected Designation of Origin (PDO) and a unique mode of consumption, making it possible to create value within the territory.
In addition, the value chain is based on pasture-based dairy production, which represents the main area of agricultural use in the country. Wooded pastures, representing historical pasture
management in the Jura mountain, predominate in the region and could help limit the negative impacts of summer drought due to the shade that helps maintain humidity. On the other hand, the
trees present suffer greatly from the drought threatening the maintenance of wooded pastures. It
is therefore interesting to understand how this territory has been able to bounce back from
economic threats and also how it can adapt to current threats caused by climate change.
